transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess… I came in because I’ve been feeling like I really messed things up for my family. We took on this mortgage, and I keep thinking I’m the reason things are harder now, like I should’ve known better.

And then at work, even little mistakes—like if I forget a table’s extra napkins or ring something in wrong—I take it as proof that I’m just useless. I know that probably sounds dramatic, but it feels like… like I deserve whatever bad stuff happens because I caused it somehow.
Have these feelings of guilt or worthlessness been present most days, even when things are going okay, or do they only come up in response to specific stressful events?

It’s… most days, I think. I mean, the mortgage thing is what I keep circling back to, because it feels like I dragged my family into this mess, even if nobody says it that way. And then at work, if I mess up something tiny, like an order or forgetting something for a table, it just kind of proves what I already feel—that I’m useless.

Even on days where nothing major happens, it’s still there in the background. Like I’m waiting for some new thing to show I deserve whatever bad comes next.
Have you noticed feeling down or losing interest in things you used to enjoy, like hobbies or time with family?

Yeah… I think it’s most days. It’s like this heavy, empty feeling in my chest, and I’m just kind of moving through things. Like at work I’m carrying plates, smiling at people, saying the usual lines because that’s what you do, not because I actually feel… anything good.

I mean, sometimes I’ll notice it in weird moments, like when a table is laughing about something and I’m standing there with the check, and I remember I used to be able to just enjoy little things like that. Now it feels more like I’m outside of it, if that makes sense.
Have you noticed feeling more tired or like you don't have the energy to get through the day, even if there's not much going on?

I don’t know… I mean, waiting tables is tiring anyway, so it’s hard to tell what’s normal and what’s me, you know? Some shifts, by the time I’m folding napkins or wiping down the station, I feel pretty worn out, but everybody does.

And then I start thinking about how some people can work doubles and still go home and do all these projects, like my cousin rebuilt his whole deck last summer after work, which I don’t even understand—sorry, that’s not really what you asked. I guess I haven’t really noticed it clearly, like “I have no energy” all the time. It’s more… I’m not sure.

Can you describe your mood throughout the day—does the heavy or empty feeling stay with you most of the time, even when nothing stressful is happening, or does it come and go depending on what’s going on around you?

It’s there most of the day, yeah. Not every single second, I guess, but most days it’s like this weight in my chest, kind of empty and heavy at the same time.

Like at the restaurant, I’ll be carrying plates around and smiling at people because that’s what you do, you know, you can’t just stand there looking miserable at table six. And sometimes I’ll catch myself doing the whole routine—“How’s everything tasting?” and all that—and I realize I don’t actually feel anything good behind it. I’m just… performing normal.

Even if nothing bad is happening right then, it’s still sort of sitting there.
How long have you been feeling this way—like most days you have that heavy, empty feeling and think negatively about yourself?

It’s been… a while. I’d say about a year, maybe a little over—like around a year and two months, if I’m trying to count it out.

I remember thinking last year, “Okay, this is just a rough patch,” because everybody has rough patches, right? And then months kept going by, and it was still there most days. The heavy feeling, and then that thing where I start blaming myself for stuff or thinking I’m just… not doing life right.

Sorry, I’m probably over-explaining. But yeah, about a year and two months.

Have there ever been times when your mood was unusually high or you felt an intense surge of energy that made you feel like you didn’t need much sleep, or where you were doing a lot more than usual—like taking on big projects or being very talkative—where others might have noticed you acting out of the ordinary?

I’m not sure. I mean, I have days where I get kind of wired at work, but that’s usually just because the dinner rush is chaos and everybody’s shouting for ranch or extra napkins or whatever.

The not sleeping thing… I don’t know. I wouldn’t say I’ve had some big stretch where I felt amazing and didn’t need sleep. Sometimes I stay up too late scrolling, but that’s not really the same, I guess.

Big projects, no. I’ll get ideas like, “I should reorganize my whole apartment,” and then I end up moving one pile of stuff and getting distracted by some old receipt from three years ago—sorry, that’s not really what you asked.

So… I don’t think so? Not anything that people have pointed out like I was acting really different.
Have you found that things you used to enjoy, like time with friends or activities you liked, feel less interesting or pleasurable to you now?

Yeah… I guess so. I mean, I used to kind of enjoy the little parts of work, like joking around with regulars. There’s this one guy who always orders the same thing and acts like he’s “still deciding,” and I used to give him a hard time about it. Now I mostly just keep my face straight and say what I need to say.

And with my brother, I used to text him after shifts, just dumb stuff, like something weird a customer said or whatever. Now I see his messages and I’ll think, “I should answer,” but then I just… don’t. It sits there. It’s not that I’m mad at him. I just don’t feel that pull to respond like I used to.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight—like eating a lot less than before or losing weight without trying?

Yeah, it’s been kind of all over the place. Some weeks at work I barely touch the staff meal, even if it’s something I usually like. I’ll just pick at it or forget it’s sitting there.

Then other nights I get home and it’s like I’m not even hungry exactly, but I’m opening cabinets and eating whatever’s there just to feel… settled, I guess. Like crackers, cereal, cold leftovers—nothing that makes sense as a meal.

I don’t know about the weight part for sure. I don’t really weigh myself much. But the eating, yeah, that’s definitely been weird.
Have you noticed that your thoughts feel slower than usual, or that you're moving more slowly, like everything is kind of dragging?

Yeah… I think people at work have noticed something like that. Not every second, but some shifts I’m kind of… buzzing around, pacing, checking the same tables or the same receipts over and over like I forgot what I just looked at.

And then other times it’s the opposite. Like grabbing menus or walking over to the POS takes me longer than it should, and I can feel myself moving like I’m in wet cement or something. It’s embarrassing, because in a restaurant you’re supposed to be quick, and if you’re slow everybody can tell.

The absence of symptoms clearly indicating adjustment disorder with depressed mood or prolonged stressor-related symptoms makes F43.22 less likely at this point.
